body.p: JAL is a high level language designed to hide the general nuisance of programming a MicroChip PIC processor. It is derived from the original JAL by Wouter van Ooijen, see: Voti
JAL is loosely based on Pascal and is not case sensitive.
This document describes the JAL syntax supported by the JALv3 compiler.

JALv3 is a fork of the JALv2 compiler. In addition to the classic PIC10/12/14/18 targets it supports PIC32 (MIPS32) and ESP32 (Xtensa LX6) devices. It extends the language with pointers, dynamic strings, fixed-capacity strings, native bit arrays, multi-dimensional arrays, wide integers up to 128 bits, optional parameters with defaults, text conversion casts, COUNT, and a cooperative task scheduler. These features are described in the chapters that follow.
This manual is maintained for JALv3 by Matthew Schinkel. The original JALv2 documentation was written by Kyle York and Rob Jansen.
